messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate (502/503) on /v1/generate from canary pool — routing now limited. Paging on-call: @alice_oncall — please investigate (see runbook: https://rwd.infr/runbooks/canary-failure)

alice_oncall: saw the alert, joining. any recent rollouts?

bob_release: pushed canary tag `service:canary-20260315` ~15m ago. no manual changes after that.

carla_sre: Grafana shows canaries spiking 502s ~5m after the rollout started. regular pool fine.

alice_oncall: quick check: `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=service -o wide` shows 6/10 canaries in CrashLoopBackOff on node g4-14. logs show image pull succeeded but process exits with `bad startup config: invalid model digest`.

bob_release: that message matches what I saw in CI: the build job pushed `service:canary-20260315` but container registry has two different digests under same tag (race during re-tag). suspect CI cache / race.

dan_ci: looking. Jenkins showed `build_and_push` retried twice due to transient registry 429; retry reused tag instead of new immutable digest — possible cache poisoning. grabbing job logs:

```
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] building image
[2026-03-15T10:13:10Z] push service:canary-20260315 -> registry.redwood.internal/service:canary-20260315
[2026-03-15T10:13:40Z] registry error 429, retry
[2026-03-15T10:14:05Z] push succeeded (same tag reused)
[2026-03-15T10:14:05Z] recorded digest sha256:abc123
```

Note later registry shows digest `sha256:deadbeef` when deployed.

alice_oncall: OK triage: impact is canary-only but traffic steering already limited; customers on prod pool unaffected at the moment. CS is watching. @fiona_cs can you confirm any customer reports?

fiona_cs: one customer reported degraded responses at 10:20 UTC but they were on canary bucket for a new internal pilot. no broader customer reports. I'm drafting a status note.

carla_sre: mitigation plan: 1) kill canary feature flag to stop routing to canaries 2) rollback canary deployments to previous stable image (stable tag `service:stable-20260301`) 3) fix CI to push immutable tag/digest and prevent re-use on retry.

alice_oncall: executing step 1 now — toggling flag `feature:canary-routing` -> off (via ff-service).

deploy-bot: feature flag `canary-routing` set to OFF by alice_oncall at 2026-03-15T10:28:03Z :white_check_mark:

bob_release: starting rollback of canary ReplicaSet to `service:stable-20260301` on the canary subset. running `kubectl -n prod set image deploy/canary service=registry.redwood.internal/service:stable-20260301` and watching.

alice_oncall: while rollback proceeds, can someone investigate registry digests? dan_ci, can you query artifact registry for tag history and the pushing job id? we need to know if tag reuse is systemic.

dan_ci: querying registry audit logs... found two pushes with same tag within 70s by job `build-#1244` (retry). Digests: `sha256:abc123` then later `sha256:deadbeef`. That matches a race where retry replaced tag. I'll open a quick patch to make retries push a new tag (append build id) and to fail if tag exists.

carla_sre: canaries are stabilizing; error rates down to baseline post-flag toggle. monitoring for 10m window then we'll close.

alice_oncall: status for pager: impact limited to canary bucket, routing turned off, rollback initiated, CI patch in progress. Severity -> SEV3. I'm going to annotate incident timeline and hand off to @bob_release for postmortem.

bob_release: taking postmortem ownership. actions noted: 1) change CI push behavior (immutable tags + digest promotion) 2) add registry enforcement to prevent tag overwrite 3) improve canary health gating (abort rollout on digest mismatch) 4) add alert when digest in deployment != registry digest for the tag.

fiona_cs: published provisional customer note for the pilot customer, CC'ing account team.

alice_oncall: logging final: `incident-bot resolve` now since canary traffic stopped, rollback applied. I'll do on-call handoff to evening shift at 18:00 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident resolved by alice_oncall at 2026-03-15T10:40:12Z — summary: canary rollout used a blurred tag (tag reused after retry) causing digest mismatch and process-level model load failures, limited to canary pool. Follow-ups assigned to bob_release/dan_ci.

bob_release: noted. I'll schedule detailed postmortem and coordinate registry policy changes. leaving channel, will DM for any follow-ups.

alice_oncall: FYI handoff to @eve_oncall_eu at 18:00 UTC — will include brief in #eng-oncall-rotations. thanks all. :thumbsup:
